entries.en: It was held late into the night every day, and the burden on the other workers increased as well. Yasuda, who was in charge of the sole, was struggling to determine the thickness of the sole. He had former track athletes, acquaintances of Ebata, try on the prototypes and gathered detailed feedback. After repeated trial and error, they would clear one challenge only to face a new wall. The number of failed prototypes exceeded 200, and after more than two months had passed...

entries.en: On a different day, in the workshop behind Kohaze-ya, the prototype machine for silk clay that welcomed Iiyama was slowly beginning to heat up. Young employees moved back and forth among the piles of cocoons stacked in cardboard boxes. The sounds of aprons and work gloves rubbing together, steam escaping, and machines humming—this morning in the factory had a slightly different atmosphere. There was a type of air that had never existed in Kohaze-ya before. Iiyama knelt beside the machine, adjusting his rubber gloves. In the back, Miyazawa was opening his notebook, watching Iiyama's movements with his eyes. Yasuda had just returned from the warehouse, carrying a bag filled with cocoons.

entries.en: For Daichi, job hunting had become an increasingly difficult task with each passing year. On a night when he stuffed yet another rejection letter into his pocket, he met up with his university classmates at a nearby izakaya for the first time in a while. Even when they clinked their mugs together, the conversation felt dampened. Complaints about their jobs and gossip about classmates who hadn’t lasted in their positions floated back and forth across the table. The sound of trains passing outside the window repeatedly interrupted and reconnected their silence. Each time, Daichi was reminded of the smell of the workshop at Kohaze-ya, his father's back, and the things he still hadn’t been able to choose.

entries.en: In the suburban track, Mogi had just finished stretching. Murano silently lowered himself and slipped his fingers into his shoes. The softness of the leather, the position of the seams, the arch of the insole—each piece of information that his fingertips could discern was something Murano would confirm with his hands before his eyes. Mogi was watching his profile intently. Although the other runners kept a slight distance, the two pretended not to notice.

entries.en: To create a sample of silk clay with the appropriate hardness for the running shoe sole, Iiyama and Daichi immersed themselves day and night without rest. Silk clay is made by boiling cocoons at high temperatures to turn them into liquid, then filtering it, and finally compressing and cooling it slowly to solidify. However, the task of controlling it to achieve the optimal hardness for the sole proved to be extremely challenging, just as Iiyama had anticipated.

The person in charge, Oohashi, was a man who showed no signs of offering the same conveniences to Kohazeya as before. Steam rose from the teacup in front of him, and that alone performed a modest welcome. Miyazawa straightened his back and restructured his explanation of Silk Ray. They ran the prototype, cooled it down, broke it apart, and then ran it again—this repetition quietly accumulated as if offering something before the memorial tablet of the late predecessor. There were no visible results yet. Still, the two of them did not stop. Iiyama glared at the numbers, while Daichi rewrote the schedule. Sleep came in fragments on the chair. What I need for that is an athlete who can deliver results immediately. I have no use for defective products!"

This veteran employee, who had been working with the abacus for many years, spoke from a position of cold detachment as he read the company's accounts. It had been a long time since he had last heard from the person on the other end, but now the only one he could rely on was this eccentric shoemaker. After the phone rang three times, a flat voice responded.

entries.en: No one had been counting how many nights they had stayed up. In front of the fifth generation Rikuou placed at the center of the workbench, everyone in the factory held their breath at the same time, their recognition aligning before they could put it into words. As Akemi dimmed the lights, the shadows of the seams emerged, and it looked less like another pair of shoes and more like a small statue that they had all enshrined together. Miyazawa pressed his fingertips to his eyes.

The dark blue fabric, inherited from his father, was imbued with a century's worth of the kohaze-ya's essence. The principles of commerce, which would never be found in an ethics textbook, were embodied in this single haori. He gently slipped his arms into the sleeves and counted the tatami seams for a while. His decision had already been made.

As he stepped off the elevator, the sound of his footsteps was absorbed by the thick carpet, and only the deep blue of the hanten he wore stood out. In the lounge where the executives of Felix were waiting, he was about to be tested on how to convey his resolve.

Now, here comes Mogi. Mogi from Daiwa Foods is moving to the front."

Even as those around him began to feel anxious, he maintained his rhythm. Miyazawa knew better than anyone the strength that lay behind that calm demeanor.

It's impressive; he still seems to have plenty of energy left. It might be a bit tough for the Japanese runners. Now, Cyrus Jui, who has won the last two years in a row, has broken away, but here comes Kozuka from Asia Industries.

entries.en: Meanwhile, at the Atlantis headquarters in Tokyo, a completely different atmosphere was prevailing. Since the broadcast of the championship race, the players' defection could no longer be hidden, and the upper management had begun to pursue the matter. Kobara, who was once supposed to serve at the pinnacle of the industry, was now on the verge of being cast down from that peak. The man who had long behaved as if the law had nothing to do with him was finally hearing the sound of his own foundation crumbling beneath him.
